newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to take YPF to court over spills.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to take YPF to court over spills.

text.p: The Argentine government will start legal proceedings against oil firm YPF for failing to obey its order issued on March 19 to shut 112 oil wells after an oil spill, officials said Tuesday.
Energy Secretary Jorge Mirkin will start the court action against Argentina's biggest listed company, government officials told local news agencies in the provinces of Neuquen and Mendoza.
No YPF official was immediately available for comment on the report.
YPF has lodged an official challenge to the Energy Secretariat's order to close the wells in Neuquen and Mendoza due to oil leaks from pipelines into the 600-mile (1,000 km) long Colorado River.
Mirkin on Monday visited the Neuquen town of Rincon de los Sauces, where the local municipality has distributed mineral water to replace the usual supply drawn from the Colorado.
YPF took out a paid advertisement in Argentine newspapers last Thursday saying that there was no safety justification to close more than 59 wells, affecting a tiny part of its production.
The company said that 25 cubic meters of crude spilled into the Colorado and that the accident was an unforeseeable result of freakish wild storms which occurred early in March and damaged pipelines.

On March 20, Neuquen's Water and Health Officer Eduardo Muller charged that YPF's oil pipelines were poorly built and in violation of international norms. He also said that the area is known for its storms and rockslides.
YPF said Monday that provincial officials who toured wells in Mendoza approved the company's precautions.
Local authorities have said thousands of cubic meters had leaked into the river, although the federal government said that that it appeared that the spillage was not that great.
